result:
Fixed. Both call sites were passing the full path bytes — including the leading NUL — to `std`'s `SocketAddr::from_abstract_name`, which prepends the NUL itself. The kernel therefore registered `\0\0aaa`, so the address read back had the extra NUL and no longer matched the requested name.

`tokio/src/net/unix/stream.rs:79` and `tokio/src/net/unix/listener.rs:83` now use `strip_prefix` instead of `starts_with`, which both detects the abstract-namespace marker and hands `from_abstract_name` the name without it:

```rust
if let Some(name) = os_str_bytes.strip_prefix(b"\0") {
    StdSocketAddr::from_abstract_name(name)?
} else {
    StdSocketAddr::from_pathname(path)?
}
```

Verification:
- `abstract_socket_name` fails before the fix (`left: [0, 97, 97]`, `right: [97, 97, 97]`) and passes after.
- Full `uds_stream` suite passes (8/8), plus `uds_datagram`, `uds_socket`, `uds_split`, `uds_cred` — all green.
- Grepped for other `from_abstract_name` call sites; these two were the only ones. `UnixDatagram` doesn't do abstract-path handling at all, so it's unaffected.

One note: to run the tests I had to temporarily comment out the `benches` workspace member, since the sandbox is offline and criterion's `anes` dependency isn't in the local cargo cache. `Cargo.toml` is restored to its original state — the only modified files are the two source files.
